docs.a: A medical website is your practice's front door online: the place where patients read about your treatments, decide whether they trust you, and call or request an appointment. docs.q: How does the website design process work?
docs.a: We follow four stages: analysis, sketch, design and development, and testing. We start by learning your goals, your budget and your taste, then assign a designer who stays with your project from the first sketch to launch. Our designers and programmers build each site from scratch in house, and people review everything before it goes live.

docs.q: How much does a medical website cost, and how long does it take to build?
docs.a: Both depend on your practice, including the number of pages, the features you need and how much content has to be created. docs.q: We already have a website. Do we need to start over?
docs.a: Not necessarily. We can review your current site to see how effective it is and recommend simple changes that suit your practice and your budget. We judge a site by whether patients can find it and whether it brings in revenue, so a full rebuild only makes sense if the existing site falls short on those points.

docs.q: How will we know if the new website is bringing in patients?
docs.a: Our results and phone tracking system lets you see the calls your website produces, so you can judge the site on patient inquiries instead of appearance alone. We cannot promise specific rankings or call volumes, since those depend on your market, your competition and the marketing you run alongside the site. What we can do is build with layouts and features that have been shown to generate results and give you a clear view of the calls coming in.

docs.a: Website accessibility means your site can be used by every patient, including people who rely on a screen reader (software that reads the page aloud), who navigate with a keyboard instead of a mouse, or who have low vision. Compliance work covers the other half: making sure forms, tracking codes and security settings treat patient information carefully. We check your site for both, fix what we find, and work with your compliance officer or attorney on anything that needs a legal decision.

docs.q: How does an accessibility audit of our current website work?
docs.a: We review your existing site against the WCAG guidelines and check how it performs for patients using screen readers, a keyboard, small phones or low vision. From there we fix the issues we find, such as contrast, headings, forms, images and keyboard navigation, and add captions to video. We also publish an accessibility statement and give patients a way to report problems.

docs.q: Will this make our website HIPAA compliant or protect us from an accessibility complaint?
docs.a: We cannot promise either, because we are a marketing agency, not a law firm. We set up contact and intake forms with HIPAA requirements in mind and build to the WCAG guidelines, which lowers the risk of a complaint but does not remove it. For legal questions, we work with your compliance officer or attorney and implement what they require.

docs.q: Why do tracking tags and pixels on our site need a review?
docs.a: Advertising and analytics tools can collect data on pages where patients share health information, such as appointment requests or intake forms, and send it to third parties. We review which tags and pixels are running on those pages so you and your compliance officer can decide what should stay, change or be removed. We also set up cookie consent and privacy policy pages so patients can see how their data is handled.

docs.q: How long does the work take, and what does it cost?
docs.a: Both depend on your practice, including the size of your site, how it was built and how many issues the audit turns up. We start with a free analysis and then give you a quote and a plan. Integration review Connection plan Built connections Automations Monitoring Documentation API Webhooks Automation platforms AI agents API Webhook Two-way sync
docs.a: An integration is a connection that lets two pieces of software share information automatically. It means the website, app, AI agents and campaigns we build can work with the systems your practice already uses, so you keep your tools and nobody has to copy data by hand. It is possible whenever your current tool offers an API or webhooks, which are the standard ways software lets other software in.

docs.q: Do we have to change our EMR or scheduling system to work with you?
docs.a: No. We start from the tools you already use and connect to them wherever they allow it. We only suggest a change when a tool cannot do something you have told us you need.

docs.q: How do we know whether our system can be connected?
docs.a: It depends on whether your vendor offers an API or webhooks and what they permit. We check that for each tool before we commit to anything, and we tell you plainly what is possible.

docs.q: What if our vendor does not offer an API?
docs.a: Then a direct connection is not possible, and we will say so. There is often a workaround, such as a scheduled export or a form that hands off to your staff, and we will explain the trade-offs.

docs.q: Is patient information safe when systems are connected?
docs.a: We use the vendor's approved methods, limit each connection to the information it needs and set everything up with HIPAA requirements in mind. Your compliance contact is involved before any patient information moves.

docs.a: Analytics and call tracking is a measurement system that records every call, form, chat and online booking your marketing produces, and shows which campaign each one came from. Without it, a practice sees its marketing bill but cannot tell which part of that spending brought in patients. With it, you can compare channels by what each inquiry cost and decide where to put your budget based on evidence.

docs.q: How does call tracking work with our existing phone number?
docs.a: We assign a separate tracking number to each marketing source, such as paid search, your Google listing or a social campaign. Calls to those numbers forward to your regular office line, so your front desk answers the phone the same way as always. Your main number stays yours, and we can see which campaign produced each call.

docs.q: Is it safe to run analytics and call recording on a medical website?
docs.a: Medical sites need more care than a typical business site, because patients may share health details in forms, chats and calls. We configure tracking so that health information patients share with you is not passed to advertising platforms. We recommend that you also review call recording and your privacy notices with your own compliance advisor, since the rules vary by state and by practice.

docs.q: What do we need to provide to get started, and how long does setup take?
docs.a: We usually need access to your website, your advertising accounts, your online booking tool and details on how calls are routed in your office. Timing depends on how many channels and systems your practice uses, so we give you a plan after a free analysis. The same applies to cost, which we quote once we have seen your current setup.

docs.q: What will we see in the reports, and will we have to interpret the data ourselves?
docs.a: You get a live dashboard you can open at any time, showing calls, form submissions, chat conversations and online bookings, along with the cost per inquiry for each channel. Each month we send a report in plain language, with AI-assisted summaries of call recordings so you learn what patients ask for. We then hold a review call with you to decide what to change next.
